bull.b: The new U.S. patent allowance strengthens protection for CAPTN-3’s modular multispecific antibody architecture and supports future development and partnering discussions. A broader, defensible IP estate can improve strategic leverage and preserve potential value as the oncology pipeline advances.

IM1240’s reported activity in treatment-resistant tumors, combined with improved safety and exposure from its masking design, addresses important limitations of existing T-cell engagers. If confirmed clinically, this differentiation could support adoption, partnerships, and a broader solid-tumor opportunity.

Minimal debt reduces refinancing and solvency pressure while the company funds ongoing research and development. Compared with a highly leveraged biotech, this provides greater flexibility to allocate available capital toward its pipeline without substantial mandatory interest or principal obligations.

bear.t: No meaningful commercial revenue and persistent losses
bear.b: The absence of meaningful revenue leaves Purple Biotech dependent on pipeline progress, partnerships, or financing rather than an established commercial base. Persistent and widening losses indicate that current research spending is not yet supported by recurring product economics, limiting earnings visibility.

bear.t: Ongoing cash burn and external funding dependence
bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow mean the company cannot currently fund development internally, even though the burn rate has moderated from prior years. Continued reliance on financing or strategic partners may constrain development choices and create funding pressure before revenue scales.

A cash runway only into mid-2027 leaves limited time to finance programs approaching clinical development, including IM1240. The need to secure partnerships or additional capital before pivotal milestones can increase execution risk and may dilute existing shareholders or narrow program priorities.
